title: Previous-year runoff reduced annual error by 8.9% after detailed weather controls at 309 Australian catchments in 2001-2021
abstract: We tested whether previous-year runoff adds information to annual runoff estimates after more detailed weather controls. We used CAMELS-AUS v2.03 at 309 Australian catchments, with 6030 test site-years in 2001-2021. Each fit used only earlier targets. Penalties were selected with validation years before 2001. Detailed controls added quarterly rain and reference evaporation, wet-day counts, five-day rain maxima and earlier late-year rain to annual weather terms. Adding previous-year square-root runoff reduced normalized mean squared error by 8.92%. The conditional 95% shared-year block interval was 7.65% to 10.34%. The median site gain was 3.50%, and 76.05% of sites improved. Complete daily runoff coverage left a 9.99% gain. A common fixed penalty left a 12.74% gain. The reduction in gain relative to annual weather controls depended on the penalty. These results show added runoff information against the tested controls. They do not identify a storage mechanism, establish drought recovery, or show lead forecast skill. Model form, source errors, selected sites and 21 test years limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, figures and reproduction instructions are included. Source observations remain external.

display.caption: Previous-year runoff reduced annual error with both control sets. Bars show conditional 95% intervals from shared three-year blocks. Site gains vary.
The runoff gain remains under complete flow coverage and a common fixed penalty. The apparent gain reduction after detailed weather controls depends on the penalty.
